categories.main_business_segments: NextEra Energy, Inc. (NEE) operates two principal business segments: Florida Power & Light Company (FPL), a rate-regulated electric utility serving Florida, and NextEra Energy Resources (NEER), which includes competitive energy and rate-regulated transmission businesses focused on clean energy generation and infrastructure across North America.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FPL's operations are based on large-scale electric generation, transmission, and distribution, utilizing a mix of natural gas, solar, nuclear, and battery storage technologies. NEER is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from wind and solar, and a leader in battery storage, employing advanced project development, construction, and operational methods for clean energy assets, as well as energy trading and risk management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: FPL primarily serves retail residential, commercial, and industrial customers in Florida, with over 5.9 million customer accounts, and a small number of wholesale customers. NEER sells energy, capacity, and related products to utilities, retail electricity providers, power cooperatives, municipal electric providers, and commercial and industrial customers across the U.S. and Canada.
categories.geographic_coverage: FPL operates throughout most of the east and lower west coasts of Florida and parts of northwest Florida. NEER operates in 41 U.S. states and 4 Canadian provinces, with generation, storage, and transmission assets distributed across North America, and a significant presence in Texas, the Midwest, West, and South regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: FPL operates as a vertically integrated, downstream utility, managing generation, transmission, and distribution to end customers. NEER is primarily a power producer (midstream/downstream), developing, owning, and operating generation and transmission assets, and also participates in upstream activities through its gas infrastructure business.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: NEE's strategic focus is on expanding clean energy leadership, investing in renewable generation, battery storage, and transmission infrastructure, and leveraging policy incentives such as the Inflation Reduction Act. R&D and innovation are directed toward cost-effective solar and wind deployment, grid modernization, hydrogen blending, and advanced storage solutions, with an emphasis on operational efficiency and customer value.
categories.revenue_model: FPL generates revenue mainly through regulated retail electricity sales, with rates set by the Florida Public Service Commission, and additional revenue from cost recovery clauses and limited wholesale sales. NEER earns revenue from long-term power purchase agreements, energy and capacity sales, renewable energy credits, commodity trading, and contracted transmission and pipeline services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FPL faces limited competition due to its regulated monopoly status but competes with self-generation and alternative energy providers. NEER competes with other independent power producers and utilities in wholesale markets, but is positioned as the global leader in wind and solar generation and a top battery storage operator, with a strong track record in project execution and long-term contracting.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: NEE reported $28.1 billion in operating revenues and $7.3 billion in net income attributable to NEE in 2023, with total assets of $177.5 billion. The company has demonstrated sustained profitable growth, with significant capital expenditures ($25.1 billion in 2023) and a robust pipeline of renewable and infrastructure projects supporting continued expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: NEE emphasizes low customer bills, high reliability, outstanding customer service, and clean energy as its core value proposition for FPL customers. For NEER, the company differentiates itself through scale, cost leadership, technological innovation, and the ability to deliver customized, reliable, and sustainable energy solutions, underpinned by long-term contracts and a strong balance sheet.
